first_impression.reaction: Our daughter sent this because the photographer quotes are all over the place and I'm paying half. I'll admit I came for a number, and the opening tells me straight away there isn't one. A bit disappointing, but it explains why, and then it does exactly what I'd do myself: get everything in writing, line by line, and find out who's responsible. Sensible, calm, no silly slang. The copyright quotes in the middle are heavy going on the iPad, and I still don't know what to pencil into the budget.

journey.quote: A single average says very little about the quote you will receive for a wedding like yours.
journey.reaction: Fair enough, but I still have to tell my husband roughly what we're putting aside. I'd have liked at least something to go on.

journey.quote: Compare quotes line by line on what is written down: hours, people, deliverables, delivery timing, licence and extras.
journey.reaction: Now that's how I'd do it. Nothing counts until it's on paper.

journey.section: Hours of coverage and the shape of your day
journey.quote: Ask how overtime is charged if the evening runs late.
journey.reaction: Good. Receptions always run late, and I don't want a surprise bill at the end of the night.

journey.quote: Ask which, and whether the figure is fixed or charged at cost afterwards.
journey.reaction: Exactly the question. 'Charged at cost afterwards' is where money disappears.

journey.quote: what happens if the photographer is ill or can't travel on the day.
journey.reaction: Thank you. That's the first thing I'd have asked. Someone thought about what goes wrong, not just the pretty part.

journey.section: Extras that sit outside the headline package
journey.quote: Album upgrades, parent albums, extra prints and framing.
journey.reaction: A parent album, yes please. But now I know it's an extra, and I've no idea what it costs.

journey.quote: who books and pays for flights, transfers and car hire, and in which currency the quote is written.
journey.reaction: Currency. Good. I don't want to be working out euros on the back of an envelope.

journey.quote: In practice, it can be difficult to get a repair, replacement or refund from an overseas business, and you should ask the consumer protection agency where the business is based whether it can help.
journey.reaction: Honest, and it's exactly what I'm frightened of. So if an Italian photographer takes our deposit and vanishes, we're on our own? I'd want to know who stands between us and that.

journey.quote: Through Wedded Concierge, one Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments with you, anywhere in the world, as your single point of contact, and confirms inclusions in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: One person, payments, in writing before we commit. That's the answer to my worry above, or part of it. I'd still want to know who's accountable if a supplier lets us down.

journey.section: Who owns the copyright in your wedding photos
journey.quote: "but, if at the time the agreement was made that person made known, expressly or by implication, to the author of the work the purpose for which the work was required, the author is entitled to restrain the doing, otherwise than for that purpose, of any act comprised in the copyright in the work."
journey.reaction: I read it twice and I'm still not sure. It's good they quote the actual Act, but a plain sentence underneath saying what it means for us would help.

journey.section: Deposits, cancellations and getting it in writing
journey.quote: Ask how the deposit and cancellation terms work, in writing, including what happens if you postpone, if the photographer cancels, and if travel is disrupted on a wedding abroad.
journey.reaction: Right questions, but it's one sentence. This is the bit I care most about and it's the shortest section on the page. Is the deposit protected or not?

journey.section: Questions to ask before you book a wedding photographer
journey.quote: Take this list into every conversation, and ask for the answers in the written quote rather than in a phone call:
journey.reaction: I'd still pick up the phone first, that's how I size people up. But yes, the answers belong in writing. I'll print this list.

journey.section: How to compare quotes in writing
journey.quote: A lower headline price with fewer hours and a slower delivery date is a different product, not a saving.
journey.reaction: That's going straight to my husband. He'll go for the cheapest quote otherwise.

journey.quote: There is no single honest figure, because a national average blends very different weddings.
journey.reaction: Said twice now. I accept it, but the page title says 'average cost', so I did expect a figure or at least a range.

journey.section: Planning the rest of the picture
journey.quote: If photography is one of many suppliers you are lining up abroad, your Wedded Advisor works in your time zone, quotes in AUD, and agrees the fee with you in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: Australian dollars, my time zone, fee in writing first. That's three of my boxes ticked in one sentence. Pity it's right at the very end.

unanswered_questions: Roughly what should we budget for a photographer, even a broad range? (business decision not to publish; flag only)
If an overseas photographer booked through the Wedded Advisor doesn't deliver or disappears with the deposit, who is accountable and are our payments protected? (deferred business detail)
Does the Wedded Advisor read and check the photographer's contract if it's in another language or currency? (deferred business detail)
Is the first conversation a phone call with a named person, and can I be included as a parent paying half? (deferred business detail)
What does the Wedded Concierge service itself cost, and when is that fee paid? (deferred business detail)

turn_offs_found.quote: There is no single honest figure, because a national average blends very different weddings.
turn_offs_found.why: I clicked on 'average cost' and there's no figure at all, not even a range. I understand the reasoning, but I can't plan a budget from 'it depends'.

turn_offs_found.quote: Ask how the deposit and cancellation terms work, in writing, including what happens if you postpone, if the photographer cancels, and if travel is disrupted on a wedding abroad.
turn_offs_found.why: Deposits are my biggest worry and this section is a single sentence, while the copyright section runs to several long quotes. The balance feels the wrong way round for someone paying.

turn_offs_found.quote: "a person makes, for valuable consideration, an agreement with another person for the taking of a photograph for a private or domestic purpose" and "the work is made in pursuance of the agreement", "the first-mentioned person is the owner of any copyright subsisting in the work by virtue of this Part".
turn_offs_found.why: Accurate, but three blocks of statute in a row are hard going on an iPad without a plain-English line after each.

would_share_with: My husband, the line about a lower headline price being a different product, not a saving, plus my question about deposit protection
My daughter, the questions-to-ask list and the seven-step quote comparison, to use with every photographer
My sister, the bit about overseas businesses being hard to get a refund from, because she's been burnt before

cta_reaction.quote: Start a conversation through Wedded Concierge, and for more planning ideas, read the Wedded Wonderland magazine.
cta_reaction.why: The sentence before it is the most reassuring thing on the page: AUD quotes, my time zone, fee agreed in writing. I'd consider it, but only if it means a phone call with a named person who can tell me who's accountable for the deposits.

top_3_changes: Expand the deposits and cancellations section into a short checklist (deposit amount and timing, refund on cancellation by either side, postponement, travel disruption), using only sourced or general guidance, so it carries the weight the copyright section does.
Add a one-line plain-English summary after each copyright quote so it can be followed on a phone or iPad.

Bring the AUD quotes, time zone and fee-in-writing reassurance up to the destination section near the first Wedded Concierge mention, and say who is accountable if an overseas supplier fails, only if the business confirms it; otherwise flag.

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Journey types limited to gained_trust, lost_trust, confused, bored, excited, objection
Stayed in character as Margaret (funding parent): read top to bottom on iPad, focused on budget, deposits, accountability, written AUD quotes and a phone call
No invented brand facts; budget range, deposit protection, Advisor contract checking, Concierge fee and first contact placed in unanswered_questions
VERIFY markers and HTML comments (fact tags, image slots, link notes) ignored
Reacted to the no-prices article as written; absence of a figure noted as a reader reaction, not a demand to invent one

open_questions.question: The deliberate no-price decision costs some trust with a paying parent who arrives on an 'average cost' keyword; does the panel want a line acknowledging budgeting (without figures)? Can the editor expand the deposits section and add plain-English lines after the copyright quotes? Can the business confirm who is accountable if an overseas supplier booked via the Advisor fails? If not, flag rather than fill.

assumptions: Margaret arrived via a link from her daughter, reading on an iPad, as a parent contributing about half the budget.

Relevance is high because photography is a direct cost she is helping fund; enquiry is moderate because the page doesn't say whether first contact is a phone call or who is accountable for deposits abroad.
Full article read top to bottom; the statute quotes were read but not fully understood.
